clue.text: Ends up as Chesil Beach, say

explanation.surface: A description of where something finishes up on the Dorset coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Chesil Beach is a long shingle bank on the Dorset coast, joined to the land at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a narrow ridge of sand or shingle running out into the sea, and Chesil Beach is a famous example.

clue.text: Burlesque? Let's change game

parts.note: a skit is a comic burlesque or parody

indicators.note: to change the word let's is to rearrange its letters

explanation.definitionFit: Skittles is a bowling game played by knocking down wooden pins, popular in British pubs.

clue.text: Charge round roof entrance on the house

explanation.surface: A builder billing for work around a loft hatch, done at no cost to the homeowner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' sounds like roofing work, but it is the idiom for something given without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the house is provided at no cost, as a free drink is from a bar.

clue.text: Conducting upbeat intro with female band

clue.text: Join lamb's rump and hog's back

explanation.walkthrough: The Hog's Back is a well-known ridge in Surrey, and hogback is a general word for such a ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge two things is to span the gap between them and so connect them.

clue.text: Ex-president one almost wishes would get thrashed in early Republican primaries

explanation.walkthrough: Primaries suggests US election contests, which suits the surface, but in the wordplay it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the 34th President of the United States, a Republican who served from 1953 to 1961.

clue.text: Tries to take in top of tight suit

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

explanation.walkthrough: Tries is the legal sense: a court tries, or hears, a case. The tailoring picture makes suit look like clothing, but it is a card suit.

clue.text: Sounds like market in which to spend time

explanation.surface: A description of a shopping venue where you might while away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing time is serving a prison sentence, so a place in which to spend time is a prisoner's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is the small room where a prisoner is held while serving their sentence.

clue.text: Rod's rude attention-seeker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a metal rod for stirring a fire
second meaning: someone who prods people to get noticed

explanation.surface: A man called Rod is described as a boorish show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod reads as a man's name, but it is the fireside tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is the iron rod used to stir a fire, and also anyone who rudely jabs others with a finger to get their notice.

clue.text: Sally crosses stage, as a form of casting

explanation.walkthrough: Sally and casting suggest the theatre; casting here means casting lots or spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by drawing lots, and more loosely sorcery, both of which involve casting lots or spells.

clue.text: Heading action needed by the one in possession?

definitions.note: a description of the document rather than a noun

parts.note: a title is a heading
a deed is an action

explanation.walkthrough: Possession and heading suggest football; the possession meant is ownership of property.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document proving ownership of land or property, which an owner needs to show their claim.

clue.text: Recruit turned Lone Ranger's head

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: first letter of Ranger

explanation.definitionFit: To recruit someone is to sign them up, which is what enrolling them means.

clue.text: African republic imprisons a church prophet

indicators.note: to imprison is to shut something inside, so one part holds the others

parts.note: Mali is a republic in West Africa
taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is the Hebrew prophet whose book is the last in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Spirit associated with a Mediterranean island

parts.note: malt whisky is a spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A liquor linked with an island in the Mediterranean Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the central Mediterranean, south of Sicily.

clue.text: Dynamic recording has a number of errors to be fixed

definitions.text: number of errors to be fixed

indicators.note: dynamic means full of movement, so the letters are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda is the Latin plural for things to be corrected, typically a list of mistakes in a printed book.

clue.text: Guardian pursuing lost sheep arrives at old city

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

explanation.walkthrough: Guardian looks like a shepherd, but it is the newspaper speaking of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the coast of what is now Turkey, famous for its Temple of Artemis.

clue.text: Sun made water race

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, or Sunday
to make water is to urinate

explanation.surface: The sun stirred up the current of a fast-flowing stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made water race' reads like a mill race; 'made water' is an old euphemism for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: To race is to go very fast, which is to speed.

clue.text: US city's on about 'optical device'

explanation.definitionFit: A laser is a device that emits a narrow, intense beam of light, so it is an optical instrument.

clue.text: Briefly against disposing of a machine separating fibre

parts.note: agin is a clipped dialect form of against
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A brief objection to scrapping a machine in a textile mill.
explanation.walkthrough: Agin is a colloquial shortening of against, as in 'I'm agin it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton gin is a machine that separates cotton fibres from their seeds.

clue.text: Kip has ball with Trotsky, military commander

O is round like a ball
Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone takes a sleep and goes to a dance with the Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Kip is British slang for a sleep. In Animal Farm the pig Napoleon drives out a rival who stands for Trotsky, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the French emperor and one of history's great military leaders.

clue.text: Oscar winner's debut lied about?

taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: Oscar looks like the film award, but it is the first name of the Irish writer.

clue.text: Doctor mingles with male unthinking followers

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A physician socialises with a man among a crowd of sheep-like followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemmings are rodents fabled to follow each other off cliffs, so the word is used for people who follow blindly.

clue.text: Right to leave a free-for-all sale

explanation.walkthrough: Free-for-all looks like part of the sale, but it is a brawl; ruction is chiefly British for an uproar.

clue.text: Cold drink? Well, that's pretty bad

rum is a drink
my! and well! are both exclamations of surprise

clue.text: Finest leasehold houses to be in sheltered position

parts.note: the run of letters inside these two words

amid means in the middle of

explanation.surface: Someone's stress is placed at the heart of an old landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: One's is the possessive pronoun, the same as your, and yr is its short form.
explanation.definitionFit: The pyramids of Egypt are among the most famous ancient monuments, built as royal tombs.

clue.text: Liverpudlian ejecting college drunkard

parts.note: Scouse means from Liverpool
C for college, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A Liverpool native throws a heavy drinker out of a college.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is the British nickname for people from Liverpool and their dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A souse is an informal word for a habitual drunk, from souse meaning to soak.

clue.text: I have an exact match for that photo

definitions.text: I have an exact match for that

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the cry in the matching card game and also a casual photograph, short for snapshot.

clue.text: Sparkler? Patience!

clue.text: Silly talk needs to be quiet

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Beloved pasta sauce's back
